text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.
LONDON - A sharp fall on Wall Street propelled British shares sharply lower as U.S. data showed stronger-than-expected inflationary pressures and heightened fears of a near-term interest rate rise.
The FTSE 100 index closed 42.5 points lower at 4,270.7, wiping out the gains of the past two sessions and leaving the index up just 34.1 points on the week.
FRANKFURT - German carmakers were the stars of the show in lacklustre bourse trade, keeping up a trend set on Thursday, with Volkswagen leading after a warmly-received analysts' meeting on Thursday.

The DAX-30 index, which measures bourse trade in German blue-chip stocks, ended down 11.44 points at 3,340.05 for a net gain on the week of 95.12. In post-bourse trade the index fell 33.34 to 3,319.24.
PARIS - French shares finished lower, with traders citing concerns over a possible further rise in U.S. interest rates.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 33.41 points at 2,574.56. The index was up 56.59 points on the week.
ZURICH - Swiss shares ended lower as price fell following U.S. data that showed a surprise jump in the core inflation rate for March.
The all-share SPI closed down 8.74 points at 2,918.14 but up 81.61 on the week.
TOKYO - The Nikkei 225 stock average ended more than two percent higher, bolstered by options settlements in the morning and buy-backs in the banking sector in the afternoon.
The Nikkei closed up 361.23 points at 17,846.98 but down 13.61 on the week.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks finished on a strong note as hopes that the market had hit a short-term bottom spurred buying in the banking sector, while China-plays also benefited from keen interest.
The Hang Seng Index closed with a gain of 157.90 points at 12,516.60, bringing the week's gains to 312.01 points.
SYDNEY - The Australian share market ended lower as cautious traders cut positions ahead of Wall Street's reaction to U.S. inflation data.
The All Ordinaries index shed 12.4 points to 2,380.5 but gained 11 points from last Friday's close.

JOHANNESBURG - A sharply weaker start on Wall Street knocked South African stocks, taking key indices to the day's lowest levels at the close. Gold stocks were largely mixed, drooping slightly towards the finish in sympathy with industrials and as bullion slipped below the $348 level.

The all-share index finished down 23.1 points at 7,022.0 for a gain of 6.2 on the week. The industrial index lost 29.4 to 8,214.3 and 24.8 from last Friday. Golds were 4.1 off to 1,306.8 but up 15.5 over the week.
